newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude ends near session low in consolidation.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude ends near session low in consolidation.

text.p: NYMEX crude ended near its session lows Monday as oil prices consolidated to create a foundation of technical support for a gasoline-led rally traditionally seen in the spring .

"We were just shaking out some weak longs in a typical consolidation," said Mike DeLuca, a dealer with Prudential Securities who was noting crude cleansed itself of positions held by uncertain traders.
April crude settled off 37 cents at $20.92 a barrel, right above its session low of $20.85.

"We could easily test $20.00, but we are setting the stage for a comeback (in crude) that takes us to $23.00 in a seasonal (gasoline) rally," said William Brown, president of W.H. Brown & Co, a trading firm in New York.
Gasoline typically rallys in the spring ahead of the summer driving season when gasoline demand peaks.
Crude led refined products lower with April gasoline finishing off 0.58 cent at 64.86 cents a gallon and April heating oil ending off 1.03 cents at 54.30 cents a gallon.
Volume suffered due to traders' attending a National Petroleum Refiners Association conference in San Antonio.
Crude's consolidation Monday was attributed to technical weakness after spot crude failed to break Friday's high of $21.45 early session Monday, rising only as high as $21.40.
"It was all a numbers game today. There was no news otherwise," said a New York crude dealer.
JP Morgan was said to be the heaviest seller late session. Officials at the brokerage were not immediately available to comment.
Despite technical weakness crude exhibited on the upside, chartists noted that prompt crude was able to hold above its simple 18-day moving average when making its session low.
Moreover, the bi-weekly CFTC Futures Commitment of Traders report as of March 11 said the large commercial players significantly increased their long positions in crude.
Energy Security Analysis Inc said in their Monday memo that the traders report indicates that spot crude may have bottomed short-term when it a hit nine-month low a little below $20.00 last week.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
